chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the 'Maf'us' (one who has been struck/killed but not yet dead), he does not inherit anything from the blood money (diyah) until he cries out and his voice is heard.

key_terms.اَلدِّيَةِ: Blood money; compensation paid to the heirs of a victim in cases of homicide or injury
key_terms.اَلْمَنْفُوسِ: The struck one; a person who has been hit or wounded but is not yet dead
key_terms.يَصِيحَ: He cries out; a loud vocalization indicating consciousness and life
key_terms.يُسْمَعَ صَوْتُهُ: His voice is heard; the audible confirmation of life required for legal status

ai.seo_question: When does a wounded person become eligible to inherit full blood money?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration in the chapter on the inheritance of the missing (Mafqud), clarifying the evidentiary threshold for distinguishing between a critically wounded individual and the deceased. By requiring an audible cry (saut), the Imam establishes a practical criterion for transferring inheritance rights, ensuring that the transition from life to death is confirmed before the distribution of blood money (diyah) begins.
